newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Avonmore says to review Waterford rejection.
newsitem.headline: Avonmore says to review Waterford rejection.

text.p: Avonmore Foods Plc told shareholders on Tuesday that its boards and management will meet on Monday next to review Waterford Foods rejection of its recent merger proposal.
"We will rule nothing in and rule nothing out," Avonmore told shareholders at an annual meeting held in Ireland's midlands city of Kilkenny on Tuesday afternoon.

It was responding to a statement by the boards of Waterford Foods Plc and Waterford Co-operative Society Limited who announced late on Friday that they could not endorse the merger proposal between the two companies as it did not reflect the underlying value of the Waterford business.
But Waterford said they agreed with the concept of merger or industry consolidation to increase shareholder value and secure the best future for all its stakeholders.
The statement followed a meeting on Friday of the two boards to consider the Avonmore offer which would have created a merged entity with turnover in excess of 2.5 billion Irish pounds.
Avonmore responded on Tuesday morning saying it was disappointed that Waterford could not endorse its merger proposals which it said had been described by a number of commentators as generous.

Avonmore did however, welcome Waterford's statement that it agreed with the concept of merger or industry consolidation. To succeed the merger must be ratified by 75 percent of Waterford Co-op (who own 68 percent of the Plc shares) and Waterford Foods Plc members.

Avonmore reiterated warnings that the food sector was facing enormous changes and challenges which could have very adverse effects on the income and livelihoods of farmer members for both organisations at its general meeting.
It said further consolidation was needed in the Irish dairy industry and that the merger with Waterford would be in the best interests of shareholders and milk suppliers for both organisations.
Avonmore, who formalised its 'friendly' offer for rival Waterford on April 14 said at that time that the proposal would go no further if it was not recommended by the Waterford boards.
